name: Context Precision
description: Whether retrieved chunks are relevant and correctly ranked
calculation: Relevant Chunks Retrieved ÷ Total Retrieved Chunks
applications: RAG chatbots, enterprise knowledge bases, documentation Q&A. Used to tune the retriever or reranker to cut irrelevant chunks
when_to_implement: As soon as a RAG pipeline reaches a working prototype, before scaling the corpus
pitfalls: Looks high while recall is low, so always measure it with recall; sensitive to chunk size
prerequisites: Relevance labels for retrieved chunks per query (human or LLM-judged)

name: Context Recall
description: Whether all needed information was retrieved
calculation: Relevant Chunks Retrieved ÷ Total Relevant Chunks Available
applications: Legal & compliance search, research assistants, KB completeness
when_to_implement: Once correctness matters more than speed, as in legal, compliance and research knowledge bases
pitfalls: Needs a labeled 'all relevant' set, which is costly; trades off against precision
tools: RAGAS, TruLens, custom eval on gold sets
prerequisites: A fully labeled set of ALL relevant chunks per query. It cannot be computed without one, and human annotation is typically required

name: Context Relevance
description: Semantic alignment between query and retrieved context
applications: Semantic search, FAQ bots, support knowledge bases
when_to_implement: During retriever/embedding selection and chunking experiments
pitfalls: Raw similarity ≠ usefulness; calibrate the threshold per embedding model
prerequisites: An embedding model; query-chunk pairs to score

name: Noise Sensitivity
description: Degradation when irrelevant content is added
applications: Large or web-scraped corpora and messy knowledge bases, where robustness against distractors matters
when_to_implement: Before scaling to large or web-scraped corpora; when retrieval mixes quality levels
pitfalls: Needs deliberate noise injection to test; results vary by noise type
tools: RAGAS, DeepEval, custom adversarial test sets
prerequisites: A clean baseline test set; a defined noise injection procedure

name: MRR (Mean Reciprocal Rank)
description: Ranking quality of the first relevant result
applications: Search engines, recommendations, 'best answer' features
when_to_implement: When a single 'best answer' is surfaced (search, top result)
pitfalls: Only credits the first relevant hit; ignores the rest of the ranking
prerequisites: A ranked retrieval system; binary relevance labels for top-k results

name: NDCG
description: Ranking quality considering graded relevance levels
applications: Graded-relevance search, e-commerce and product search, document ranking
when_to_implement: When results carry graded relevance (e-commerce, document ranking)
pitfalls: Requires graded relevance labels; sensitive to cutoff k
prerequisites: Graded (multi-level) relevance labels per result, which take more annotation effort than binary labels. Agree on the scale first

name: Faithfulness
description: Whether the response is grounded in the provided context
applications: RAG assistants and medical or financial summarizers, to prevent fabricated claims
when_to_implement: First quality metric to add once a RAG system answers users
pitfalls: LLM-judge scoring is noisy; define 'claim' granularity clearly. Measures support by the given context, not truth: a faithful answer to wrong context is still wrong. Report it with its standard error over the test set, not as a bare number
prerequisites: Source context must accompany each answer; a claim extraction method (LLM-based or rule-based). If an LLM judge scores it: its agreement rate with human raters, measured on a sample of your own data

name: Answer Relevance
description: Whether the answer addresses user intent
calculation: Mean relevance over a test set, by one stated method: either the mean embedding similarity between the question and questions an LLM generates from the answer (the RAGAS method), or a rubric score (for example 1 to 5) from an LLM judge or a human rater. The two methods do not give comparable numbers
applications: Consumer chatbots, virtual assistants, support deflection
when_to_implement: Any user-facing assistant or chatbot
healthy_target: ≥ 4/5 for a rubric score; for the embedding method, set a baseline per system
pitfalls: Relevant ≠ correct; can score high on fluent-but-wrong answers. In its own paper the RAGAS method agreed with human raters in 78% of pairwise comparisons, against 95% for faithfulness
prerequisites: A test query set with defined intent; an LLM judge or human raters. If an LLM judge scores it: its agreement rate with human raters, measured on a sample of your own data

name: Answer Correctness
applications: QA systems, tutoring/edtech, model benchmarking
when_to_implement: When ground truth exists (QA, benchmarks, edtech)
pitfalls: Needs maintained gold answers; partial-credit scoring is tricky. Report it with its standard error over the test set, not as a bare number
prerequisites: A maintained gold-answer dataset per question, curated continually as the system evolves. If an LLM judge scores it: its agreement rate with human raters, measured on a sample of your own data

name: Citation Precision
description: Whether the citations given actually support the claims they are attached to (citation precision; see M43 for recall)
applications: Research tools, regulated industries, 'show your sources' features
when_to_implement: When you expose sources or operate under compliance/traceability needs
pitfalls: A citation existing ≠ supporting the claim; verify the link, not just presence
prerequisites: Output must include structured citations; source content must be accessible for claim-level verification

name: Semantic Similarity
description: Similarity between generated and reference answers
calculation: Mean cosine similarity between the embeddings of each generated answer and its reference answer, over a test set
applications: Summarization/paraphrase evaluation, regression testing
when_to_implement: Regression-testing outputs across model or prompt changes
pitfalls: High similarity can mask factual errors; embedding-model dependent. Compare scores only within one embedding model. Token-level methods such as BERTScore give different numbers
prerequisites: A reference answer per test query; an embedding model

name: Prompt Success Rate
description: Percentage of prompts producing acceptable output
applications: Prompt library QA, prompt versioning, agent prompt tuning, A/B testing
when_to_implement: Once you maintain a prompt library or version prompts
pitfalls: 'Acceptable' must be defined precisely or the number is meaningless
prerequisites: A written definition of 'acceptable output'; a versioned prompt library or test harness

name: Prompt Injection Detection Rate
applications: Public-facing chatbots, agent guardrails, LLM firewalls
when_to_implement: Before exposing an LLM/agent to untrusted user input
pitfalls: Attack patterns evolve; static test sets go stale fast
tools: Rebuff, LLM Guard, Garak, custom red-team sets
prerequisites: A curated adversarial prompt test set, updated regularly as attack patterns evolve

name: Toxicity Score
description: Harmful or offensive content in outputs
applications: UGC/social moderation, consumer chatbots, brand-safety filtering
when_to_implement: User-generated content or open-ended consumer chat
pitfalls: Classifiers carry bias; context can flip toxicity judgments
prerequisites: A toxicity classifier or API access (Perspective API, Detoxify, or equivalent)

name: Safety Violation Rate
applications: Policy-compliance monitoring, content platforms, enterprise gating
when_to_implement: Before enterprise/regulated deployment; ongoing in production
pitfalls: Depends on a clear, enforced policy taxonomy
tools: LLM Guard, Guardrails AI, NeMo Guardrails
prerequisites: A written, enforced policy taxonomy; a classification system or human review queue

name: Refusal Accuracy
applications: Consumer assistants, child-safety, jailbreak resistance
when_to_implement: Consumer assistants and safety-critical surfaces
pitfalls: Over-refusal hurts UX; measure false refusals too
tools: Custom safe/unsafe eval sets, red-teaming, LLM-as-judge
prerequisites: A labeled dataset of safe/unsafe inputs with expected model behavior per prompt

name: Latency (P50/P95/P99)
applications: Real-time chat, voice assistants, SLA monitoring, UX tuning
when_to_implement: From day one of any real-time/interactive deployment
pitfalls: Averages hide tail pain; always track P95/P99, not the mean
prerequisites: Request-level timing instrumentation; an observability stack

name: Token Consumption
applications: Cost forecasting, context-window optimization, local LLM resource planning
when_to_implement: As soon as usage scales or you run local LLMs on fixed budgets
healthy_target: Set per system: a token budget per task, with usage flat or falling while quality holds
pitfalls: Output tokens often dominate cost; context bloat creeps up
prerequisites: Token counting at the inference layer; provider billing or logging API access

name: Cost per Request
applications: Pricing & margin analysis, model selection (cloud API vs local LLM)
when_to_implement: When choosing between models or cloud API vs local hosting
healthy_target: Set per system: at or below the cost per request assumed in the business case
pitfalls: Excludes retrieval/infra/human-review cost if measured naively
tools: Provider billing, Helicone, LangSmith, custom tracking
prerequisites: Token consumption data; provider unit pricing; infra cost attribution if self-hosted

name: Tool Call Success Rate
applications: AI agents, function/tool calling, API automation, copilots
when_to_implement: First agent metric to add once tools/function calling are live
pitfalls: Conflates model errors with flaky external APIs; separate them
prerequisites: A live tool/API environment; request-level logging with success/failure outcomes

name: Agent Task Completion Rate
applications: Autonomous agents, workflow automation, RPA, task copilots
when_to_implement: When agents run multi-step tasks end-to-end
pitfalls: 'Completion' needs an objective success definition per task
tools: LangSmith, custom task harness, human eval
prerequisites: Defined success criteria per task type; end-to-end execution logs

name: Agent Handoff Success Rate
applications: Multi-agent systems, orchestration, supervisor/worker pipelines
when_to_implement: Multi-agent or orchestrated systems
pitfalls: Context loss at handoff is the usual failure; trace state transfer
prerequisites: Multi-agent infrastructure with handoff state logging; context payload captured at each transfer

name: Planning Accuracy
applications: Planning agents, multi-step reasoning, task decomposition
when_to_implement: Agents that decompose tasks or generate multi-step plans
pitfalls: A valid plan ≠ successful execution; judge plan quality carefully
prerequisites: Reference plans or success criteria per task type; a plan evaluation method

name: Memory Retrieval Accuracy
applications: Personal assistants, long-running agents, conversational memory
when_to_implement: Long-running agents or assistants with persistent memory
pitfalls: Stale or conflicting memories degrade accuracy over time
tools: Vector DB eval, Mem0, custom memory benchmarks
prerequisites: A persistent memory store; labeled ground-truth memory items per test case

name: Data Classification Accuracy
applications: Data catalogs, DLP, automated sensitivity labeling, compliance
when_to_implement: When automating sensitivity labeling or catalog tagging
pitfalls: Class imbalance inflates accuracy; check per-class metrics
prerequisites: A labeled ground-truth sample covering all sensitivity classes; representative of your actual data distribution

name: PII Detection Recall
applications: Privacy compliance (GDPR/CCPA), redaction pipelines, anonymization
when_to_implement: Any pipeline handling personal data (GDPR/CCPA)
pitfalls: Favor recall over precision here; rare PII types get missed
tools: Presidio, cloud DLP services, spaCy NER
prerequisites: A fully human-annotated dataset with ALL PII instances labeled. Recall cannot be estimated without knowing the true total

name: PII Detection Precision
applications: Redaction tuning, to avoid over-redaction
when_to_implement: Alongside recall, when over-redaction harms data utility
pitfalls: Tuning up recall drops precision; balance to the use case
tools: Presidio, cloud DLP services, custom validation
prerequisites: The same labeled dataset as PII Detection Recall (M27), since both metrics share one annotation requirement

name: Data Quality Rule Coverage
description: Percentage of critical data covered by rules
applications: Data governance programs, data contracts, pipeline monitoring
when_to_implement: When standing up a data governance program or data contracts
pitfalls: Coverage ≠ passing; track rule pass rate too
tools: Great Expectations, dbt tests, Soda, Monte Carlo
prerequisites: An inventory of critical data elements; a rules engine (dbt, Great Expectations, or Soda)

name: Metadata Completeness
applications: Data catalog maturity, asset discoverability
when_to_implement: When building or maturing a data catalog
pitfalls: Filled ≠ accurate; completeness can hide stale metadata
tools: Data catalog platforms, OpenMetadata, custom audits
prerequisites: A data catalog with defined required fields per asset type

name: Lineage Coverage
applications: Impact analysis, audit & compliance, root-cause debugging
when_to_implement: When impact analysis or audit/compliance is required
pitfalls: Column-level lineage is much harder than table-level
tools: OpenLineage, catalog platforms, dbt exposure graphs
prerequisites: A lineage tracking tool (OpenLineage, catalog platform); a complete asset inventory

name: Explainability Score
applications: Regulated AI (finance/healthcare), model risk management, audit
when_to_implement: Regulated or high-stakes AI (finance, healthcare)
healthy_target: 100% of consequential decisions explainable to the person who acts on them; set the threshold for other outputs per system
pitfalls: Explanations can be plausible but unfaithful to the model
tools: SHAP, LIME, model cards, LLM rationale checks
prerequisites: A context-specific definition of 'explainable' agreed with stakeholders; access to model internals or structured rationale output

name: Model Drift Score
applications: Production ML monitoring, retraining triggers, MLOps
when_to_implement: Once a model is in production serving real traffic
pitfalls: Drift signal ≠ performance drop; confirm against outcomes
prerequisites: A baseline prediction distribution from a reference/training window; ongoing prediction logging

name: Data Drift Score
applications: Input/feature monitoring, drift alerts, data pipeline health
when_to_implement: Production monitoring of input/feature distributions
pitfalls: Seasonal shifts trigger false alarms; set sensible baselines
tools: Evidently, Arize, WhyLabs, custom KS/PSI checks
prerequisites: A baseline input distribution from a reference window; a feature logging pipeline

name: Availability/Uptime
applications: SLA/SLO tracking, production reliability, enterprise services
when_to_implement: Any production service with reliability expectations
pitfalls: Define 'available' precisely (does degraded count?)
prerequisites: A health-check endpoint; an uptime monitoring tool with alerting

name: Error Rate
applications: Reliability monitoring, incident detection, release health
when_to_implement: From first production release
pitfalls: Silent/soft failures (bad answers) aren't caught by HTTP errors
prerequisites: Request-level logging with error classification (model errors vs. infra errors vs. silent failures)

name: Human Override Rate
applications: Human-in-the-loop systems, autonomy calibration, trust measurement
when_to_implement: Human-in-the-loop or assisted-decision systems
healthy_target: Set per system against a baseline; investigate sustained rises, and treat a rate near zero as a sign reviewers may have stopped checking
pitfalls: Very low can mean rubber-stamping, not high quality
prerequisites: A human-in-the-loop workflow with logged override events and decision IDs

name: User Satisfaction Score
applications: Consumer apps, support CSAT, product feedback loops
when_to_implement: Once real users interact with the product
pitfalls: Low response rates bias results; pair with behavioral signals
tools: In-app surveys, thumbs up/down, CSAT tools
prerequisites: An in-product feedback mechanism (ratings, thumbs, surveys) surfaced at the right moment

name: Business Outcome Lift
applications: ROI and business cases, executive reporting, value realization
when_to_implement: When justifying ROI or reporting value to stakeholders
healthy_target: Positive lift against a baseline set in advance, statistically significant (for example p < 0.05 in an A/B test)
pitfalls: Attribution is hard; needs a control/baseline to be credible
tools: A/B testing platforms, BI dashboards, experiment frameworks
prerequisites: A defined baseline KPI; a control group or pre/post measurement window; a statistical test plan

name: Time to First Token (TTFT)
description: Time until the first output token is returned
calculation: Timestamp of First Token − Request Start
applications: Streaming chat UX, voice agents, perceived responsiveness
when_to_implement: Streaming chat/voice UX where perceived speed matters
pitfalls: Good TTFT can still mask slow total completion; track both
prerequisites: Streaming responses enabled; token-level timestamp logging at the API or inference layer

name: Adoption Rate
description: Share of eligible users actively using the AI
applications: Internal tool rollout, change management, product-led growth
when_to_implement: When rolling out an internal or consumer AI tool
healthy_target: Set per system: rising toward the active-user share named in the business case
pitfalls: The active-user definition drives the number; avoid vanity metrics
prerequisites: User identity tracking; a clear agreed definition of 'active' and 'eligible' users

name: Audit Trail Coverage
description: Portion of AI decisions with a complete audit record
applications: Compliance & audit, regulated deployments, forensic review
when_to_implement: Regulated deployments or anything needing decision forensics
pitfalls: Logs without enough context aren't truly auditable
tools: Immutable logging, SIEM, MLflow tracking, audit platforms
prerequisites: An immutable logging system; a defined list of which decisions are 'consequential' and what context each log must capture

name: Citation Recall
description: Whether each statement in the answer is fully supported by the passages it cites
calculation: Statements fully supported by their cited passages ÷ total statements in the answer (a statement with no citation counts as unsupported)
example: 18 of 20 statements supported by their citations = 90%
applications: Research tools, regulated industries, 'show your sources' features
when_to_implement: When you expose sources or operate under compliance/traceability needs; measure it alongside citation precision (M10)
healthy_target: Set per system against a baseline; give it priority over citation precision, since an unsupported statement misleads more than an extra citation
pitfalls: Support is judged by an entailment model or an LLM judge, and a yes/no support check misses partial support. High recall with low precision buries the useful sources among irrelevant ones
tools: Entailment (NLI) models such as the T5 TRUE model used by the ALCE benchmark, LLM-as-judge, custom claim-citation verifiers
prerequisites: Answers whose statements carry citations to retrievable passages; a support judgment per statement. If an LLM judge scores it: its agreement rate with human raters, measured on a sample of your own data

name: Factual Precision
description: Share of the atomic facts in an answer that a reliable knowledge source supports, independent of the context the system was given
calculation: Atomic facts supported by the knowledge source ÷ total atomic facts in the answer
applications: Consumer assistants, long-form answers, any system that answers from its own knowledge rather than only from retrieved context
when_to_implement: Any high-trust answer surface; track from first production release. Use faithfulness (M07) when the question is whether answers stay within the given context
healthy_target: Set per system against a baseline; no general threshold is established
pitfalls: Only as good as the knowledge source and the fact-splitting step: facts the source does not cover count as unsupported. It answers a different question from faithfulness, and the two are often confused when hallucination data is labeled
tools: FActScore, LLM-as-judge with retrieval, custom fact verifiers
prerequisites: A reliable knowledge source covering the answer's domain; a method that splits answers into atomic facts. If an LLM judge scores it: its agreement rate with human raters, measured on a sample of your own data
